name: Andreas von Bechtolsheim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Andreas "Andy" von Bechtolsheim is cofounder and chief architect of network switching company Arista Networks.

Born in Germany, Bechtolsheim studied computer engineering at Carnegie Mellon University and dropped out of a Stanford Ph.D. program in 1982 to cofound Sun Microsystems with Bill Joy, Scott McNealy and Vinod Khosla.
Much of his fortune stems from an early $100,000 investment in Google.
He cofounded Arista in 2004 and owns a nearly 17% stake in the business, which he has earmarked for his heirs.
Following SEC insider trading charges, Bechtolsheim agreed in 2024, without admitting guilt, to a five-year ban on serving as an director or officer of Arista or any public company.
forbes_facts: Besides Arista, Bechtolsheim cofounded two other IT networking companies with David Cheriton (one sold to Sun Microsystems, another to Cisco).
Bechtolsheim invented one of the first network workstations while studying for a Ph.D.

name: Mike Adenuga
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Mike Adenuga built his fortune in telecommunications and oil production.
His mobile phone network, Globacom, is the third-largest operator in Nigeria, with more than 17 million subscribers.
His oil exploration outfit, Conoil Producing, operates 6 oil blocks in the Niger Delta.
Globacom also built Glo-1, a 6,100-mile-long submarine Internet cable to the U.K. via Ghana and Portugal.
Adenuga also owns 74% of publicly traded gasoline firm Conoil and just under 6% of publicly traded Nigerian bank Sterling Financial Holding.
forbes_facts: Adenuga got an MBA at Pace University in New York, supporting himself as a student by working as a taxi driver.
Adenuga  made his first million at age 26 selling lace and distributing soft drinks.

name: Mário Araripe
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Mario Araripe founded Brazil's largest renewable energy developer Casa dos Ventos, meaning "House of the Winds," in 2007.
Araripe is the majority owner of the privately held company and currently shares its leadership roles with his son Lucas Araripe.
Before turning to renewables, he helmed companies in the real estate, textile, and car industries;  in 2006, he sold off-road vehicle manufacturer Troller to Ford.
French company TotalEnergies acquired a 34% stake in Casa dos Ventos' energy generation portfolio in 2023, with the joint venture valued at over $2 billion.
Casa dos Ventos' developments account for one-third of all Brazilian wind farms currently in operation.
forbes_facts: Raised in the northeastern state of Ceará, Araripe returned to the windy plateaus of his homeland to develop Casa dos Ventos' first projects.

name: Femi Otedola
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2009-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Femi Otedola is a Nigerian billionaire who made his first fortune in commodities before selling his shares in Forte Oil to invest in the energy business.
In 2025, Otedola sold his majority stake in Geregu Power, a power generation business, pocketing roughly $750 million.
He had previously sold down his stake in Geregu, which once exceeded 95%, to bring on institutional investors.
He retains a 5% stake in the Lagos-based company.
He also owns properties in Lagos, Dubai, London and Monaco, and holds shares in Zenith Bank and FBN Holdings.
forbes_facts: His daughter is a professional DJ who goes by the stage name DJ Cuppy.

name: Igor Yusufov
forbes_bio: Igor Yusufov is the founder of Energy Corporation, which invests in oil and gas, mining and infrastructure companies.
In the early 1990s, Yusufov was a deputy secretary of Foreign Economic Relations.
From 2001 to 2004, he was the Russian Federation's energy minister.
He also served on the board Russian gas giant Gazprom from 2003 to 2013.

name: Robert Coyiuto Jr.
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2020); Hurun Global (2020-2023)
forbes_bio: Robert Coyiuto Jr. is the chairman of privately held Prudential Guarantee and Assurance, one of the largest non-life insurance companies in the Philippines.
The company was founded by his late father Robert Sr., who was the first Filipino to become an underwriter of Lloyd's of London, a world-leading insurance market.
He also owns a stake in privately held National Grid and listed Oriental Petroleum & Minerals.
forbes_facts: He founded PGA Cars in 1996, which is the sole distributor of Audi, Porsche, Lamborghini and Bentley in the Philippines.
His Coyiuto Foundation set up a biennial award in 2014 for authors of biographies and autobiographies.
In 2021, Coyiuto increased his holding in listed Synergy Grid following a share swap with his investment firm Pacifica21.
